A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SANER and provide readable main text, Equations 1-13, Tables 1-10, Figures 1-6, and Appendices A-G. The complete material supports reliable comparison despite changes in pagination and citations.

before.justification: v2 reports original retrieval, classification, and image-generation experiments in Sections 4-5, with ablations, additional benchmark results, and image-quality measurements in Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including numerical comparisons in Tables 1-10 and generated-image examples in the main text and Appendix E.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same attribute neutralization, residual MLP, debiasing and regularization losses, and training and inference procedures. No method component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions retain COCO training, FairFace/PATA/FACET retrieval evaluation, ImageNet-1K classification, and image generation including COCO Karpathy evaluation. The protected attributes and neutral versus explicit-attribute prompt scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Original CLIP, Prompt (Berg et al., 2022), Projection (Chuang et al., 2023), and SANER. Comparator membership also matches in the age/race, classification, generation, BLIP, and FACET comparisons. Newly cited works are not added baselines.

E3.justification: Dataset sizes, training budgets, backbones, prompt templates, metrics, and generation sample counts remain unchanged, including the appendix protocols. The small wording deletion in the MaxSkew description does not alter Equation 12 or its evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: The loss-component ablations in Table 7, data-size sensitivity in Table 8, image-quality checks in Appendix B.4, and generation case studies in Figures 3-6 are retained without revision.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point estimates and averaging practices. Neither reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1-10 and the FID/CLIPScore results in Appendix B.4 match. Generated-image examples and reported findings also match; for example, SANER retains 65.2% ImageNet accuracy and 0.39 statistical parity.

T1.justification: Equations 1-13 and their associated definitions and mathematical reasoning are unchanged. The wording edit surrounding MaxSkew does not revise its mathematical definition, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract omits two sentences about avoiding retraining and applying debiased CLIP to image generation. These claims remain in the Introduction and Section 5; the central contributions and their scope are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 6 and Appendices F-G retain the same discussion of residual bias, intersectional and non-binary extensions, predefined attribute words, and potential overconfidence. Interpretations of regularization and training-data diversity in Appendix B also remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures are unchanged, including the 128-dimensional hidden layer, batch size 128, learning rate 5e-6, A100 hardware, and five-hour training time. Attribute dictionaries, prompt lists, preprocessing information, and the project-page link are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds Yamazaki et al. (2022, 2023), Garcia et al. (2023), and Hirota et al. (2024a, 2024b), while removing Zeng et al. (2023) and Wang et al. (2019). These are limited citation updates in the Introduction, binary-gender footnote, and Related Work; the substantive positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract loses its final two sentences, the publication header and author/correspondence text receive small edits, and the MaxSkew description loses a short phrase. Section order and nearly all explanatory prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 moves from page 6 to page 5, and surrounding text and existing tables reflow. Figure and table designs, captions, and image examples are retained. Appendix page bodies are visually identical apart from the updated publication headers.

improvement.justification: The shorter abstract trades immediate visibility of the no-retraining and generation claims for concision, while retaining those claims in the body. Citation updates and modest reflow leave the technical exposition, empirical support, reproducibility information, and limitations essentially unchanged. These limited editorial changes produce no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
